newsitem.title: USA: Avon sees emerging markets growth.
newsitem.headline: Avon sees emerging markets growth.

text.p: Avon Products Inc president Edward Robinson said he expects Avon's current sales growth in emerging markets of between 10 percent and 12 percent to continue for several more years as the company expands into Vietnam, Burma and South Africa in 1997.
"Substantial growth is coming from emerging markets, especially Asia," said Robinson, who is also the chief operating officer. "That percentage will continue to grow for a while."

The company said its developing markets generated 38 percent of Avon sales and 49 percent of pre-tax profits in 1995. Robinson did not say whether contributions from developing markets are expected to grow as a percentage of total corporate results.

Avon posted third-quarter earnings of $0.47 per share compared to $0.41 per share. Sales for the quarter increased to $1.18 billion from $1.07 billion last year, with international sales rising 10 percent.
Robinson declined to comment on specific earnings estimates going forward.
The consensus analysts' 1996 share earnings estimate from First Call is $2.37. For 1997, the estimate is $2.72 per share.

"It's a terrific market for direct selling," he said of the developing world. "We provide an opportunity for people." Since 1990, Avon Products Inc has entered 14 new countries to market its cosmetics, fragrances and toiletries by direct sale. India, the world's second most populated country, is the latest new frontier.

In New Delhi, about 20 Indian women have been recruited so far to sell to their family and friends and rely on regional branch stores in a modified direct selling approach Avon has deployed with good results in the Phillipines and China.
Robinson said it was too early to predict sales growth from India, but was positive about the sizeable middle class in the population of 900 million.
"It's a really great market," said Robinson. "We think that India has great long- term possibilities."
The company said it expects to have 50,000 representatives in India by the year 2000. After Vietnam and South Africa, he said the company will be ready for the next new market.
"There are a number of places we have yet to go," Robinson said without citing specific targets.
